3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Defacto complainant.
Perused the material on record.
4.
Respondent No.2 lodged a complaint reporting missing of his minor daughter aged about 16 years 4 months from NC:2023:KHC:25272 14.03.2023.

On the basis of the said complaint,
Cr.No.64/2023 was registered against the petitioner under Section 363 of Indian Penal Code.
The victim girl was secured on 24.03.2023 and her statements under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., as well as under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., were recorded.

The charge sheet is filed against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Sections 366 & 376(2)(n) of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 5(l)
and 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

6. The statement of the victim reveal that the petitioner and the victim were together in the house of CWs.9 and 10 from 14.03.2023 till 24.03.2023.
In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has not alleged any NC:2023:KHC:25272 sexual assault committed against her by the petitioner.
She has stated that she is in love with the petitioner and coming to know about their love affair, her parents did not allow her to attend the college.
Therefore, she went along with the petitioner and stayed with him in his sister's house for ten days.
The victim has also refused to undergo medical examination.

7. As per prosecution, the date of birth of the victim is 10.11.2006 and therefore it is contended by the learned High Court Government Pleader that the victim is a minor as on the date of commission of the offence.

However, considering that the victim has not alleged any sexual assault committed against her in the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the prosecution has to establish its case during full pledged trial.
Investigation is completed and the charge sheet is filed.
8. Considering the above facts and circumstances, petitioner can be released on bail by imposing certain conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
NC:2023:KHC:25272 ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused in Crime No.64/2023 of Sampigehalli Police Station, pending in Spl.C.C.No.918/2023 on the file of the FTSC IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, shall be released on bail subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
b) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
